scope: The fourteen reserved original P3 goals, with source ordinals exactly as in root-model-source-allocations.tsv. Native source reconstructions remain distinct from common editorial results and examples.

setup: Complete first-order theories in countable signatures, with an infinite model for the omega-categorical equivalence
Complete finite-tuple types, isolation, compactness and the countable omitting-types construction

components.text: State all equivalent finite-n-type, isolated-type and unique countably infinite model conditions, with the finite-model and countable-language boundaries explicit.
Prove the characterization in both directions: the finite-type realization/back-and-forth construction and the nonisolated-type omission or equivalent source-native obstruction.
Present Engeler's actual 1959 p. 161 announcement and its qualifications; identify its contribution without inventing an absent long proof.
Give the DLO type/order-pattern calculation, extension argument and unique countable model example under the language without endpoints.
Give the random-graph finite-type and extension-axiom example, applying the corrected finite-signature/no-function hypotheses to the Fraisse application.
Compare the three original attributions and the corrected textbook presentation, retaining each source's stated result and proof extent.

profiles.failure: One implication or finite-tuple case is absent, the Engeler abstract is credited with a fabricated proof, or Hodges's corrected application hypotheses are omitted.

related.reason: The graph example uses the separately allocated Fraisse construction; no reverse proof dependency is inferred.
Type isolation and countable model constructions share definitions and must use the same finite-parameter conventions.

setup: Countable relational signature and a countable set of isomorphism types of finite structures with unbounded size
Embeddings of finite substructures, HP, JEP and AP; direct unions and countable scheduling

components.text: Define age, embedding and ultrahomogeneity and state the exact HP/JEP/AP countability and unboundedness conditions.
Construct the increasing sequence meeting every finite extension requirement and verify well-definedness, countability and its exact age.
Prove the extension property and both directions of the countable back-and-forth uniqueness and ultrahomogeneity arguments.
Construct the countable graph and derive every finite disjoint adjacency/nonadjacency extension instance, then prove uniqueness and universality in the correct embedding sense.
Supply explicit finite amalgamation examples and an AP failure example, distinguishing structural maps from partial elementary maps.
Apply the 2011 p. 352 correction only to the textbook categoricity application and show why countable-signature limit existence alone gives no general omega-categoricity conclusion.

profiles.failure: An unscheduled extension case is omitted, a homomorphism is substituted for an embedding, or existence/uniqueness is asserted from an outline alone.

related.reason: The categorical graph application is separately mapped and must not become a circular prerequisite of limit existence.

setup: Countable complete theory, finite tuple types and countable elementary chains
Atomicity, isolation density and omitting types; saturation over finite parameter sets

components.text: Define prime, atomic, saturated and homogeneous models with tuple, parameter and cardinal scopes explicitly distinguished.
Prove that a countable model is prime exactly when atomic and that prime models exist exactly when isolated types are dense, including the embedding construction.
Prove that a countable complete infinite theory has a countable saturated model exactly when every finite-n type space is countable, by the full chain construction.
Prove countable saturated-model uniqueness and the appropriate extension/homogeneity property by back-and-forth.
Work through DLO, the relevant prime/atomic example and a type-isolation obstruction, retaining finite-model edge cases and distinguishing smallness from omega-stability.

profiles.failure: Countable-model hypotheses disappear, saturation over finite parameters is replaced by saturation over countable sets, or smallness is incorrectly identified with omega-stability.

setup: Complete first-order theory in a countable language and countable-model isomorphism spectrum
Prime/atomic and countable saturated model constructions; descriptive set-theoretic formulations where explicitly used

components.text: State and prove Vaught's never-two theorem with the complete countable-model construction and all cases.
Give the exact original conjecture formulation and distinguish it from the proved never-two result.
Reconstruct Morley's actual 1970 more-than-aleph-1 threshold theorem and its proof, preserving its countable/infinitary language regime.
Distinguish cardinal dichotomy, perfect-set, infinitary and omega-Vaught formulations, including what CH does to a mere cardinal formulation.
Provide a dated 9 September 2026 status paragraph checked against the selected August 2026 primary version, separating restricted recent results from the general conjecture.

profiles.failure: A never-two or restricted Scott-rank result is presented as solving the general conjecture, or a cardinal formulation is conflated with its perfect-set strengthening.

related.reason: Shared prime/atomic model definitions and construction lemmas must be identified before their actual use in the source proof.

additional.extent: The v2 abstract, introduction and precise current-status/variant statements necessary for the dated status paragraph; no automatic full new-paper reconstruction.

setup: Countable theory with a distinguished unary predicate U and a model with |M| > |U| >= aleph-0
Elementary diagrams, chains, Vaught pairs and recursive saturation as actually used by the chosen proof

components.text: State the basic transfer to a model of cardinal pair (aleph-1, aleph-0) with the language, infinitude and strict-cardinality hypotheses.
Reconstruct the 1965 Cardinals Far Apart construction at its actual theorem scope and distinguish any stronger gap transfer from the basic displayed claim.
Define recursive saturation and the exact Vaught-pair ingredients needed by the third edition's proof and supply all construction and union steps.
Compare the original and third-edition methods and give a valid cardinal-pair application without substituting Chang's elementary-submodel conjecture.

profiles.failure: A countability, infinitude or cardinal-gap hypothesis is missing, or an elementary-submodel conjecture or different presentation is used as the proof of the selected theorem.

setup: Complete countable theory, saturation sufficient for parameter sets and definable families
Ordinal rank recursion, finite multiplicity, algebraic closure and strongly minimal pregeometry

components.text: Define Morley rank, total transcendence and finite rank degree and prove the countable-theory connection with omega-stability.
Supply Morley's complete categoricity-in-one-uncountable-cardinal to every-uncountable-cardinal proof, including its hard existence and transfer lemmas.
Prove the strongly minimal algebraic-closure pregeometry, exchange and basis dimension results with parameter scope explicit.
Supply the strongly minimal coordinatization/existence and prime-over-basis constructions required by the Baldwin-Lachlan refinement.
Derive the source's countable-model consequences and distinguish dimension, rank and degree throughout the classification.
Give the algebraically closed field illustration with fixed characteristic and separate the original Morley method from later refinements.

profiles.failure: A hard existence/coordinatization step remains a citation or sketch, one uncountable cardinal is silently replaced by a finite/countable case, or rank, degree and basis dimension are conflated.

related.reason: Prime models over named parameter sets require their own extension of the earlier countable model package.

setup: Complete theory and a sufficiently saturated homogeneous ambient model with explicitly bounded parameter sets
Formula order property, cardinal type counts, dividing and forking over specified bases

components.text: Define stability in a cardinal, stability, superstability and omega-stability and state the full selected stability-spectrum conditions and invariants.
Supply the 1978 first edition's selected stability-spectrum proofs and their exact cardinal-arithmetic and local-character hypotheses.
Define dividing and forking and prove the selected stable nonforking extension, symmetry and transitivity laws with all base/ambient restrictions.
Give the geometric formulation of independence and compare it with the source's type-based calculus without assigning unsupported spectrum claims to Pillay.
Prove the hierarchy implications and provide the required strictness examples with the source-specific properties justified.
Build the spectrum and independence lookup entries and explain which simple-theory generalizations require the separate N-a-010 treatment.

profiles.failure: The revised 1990 book replaces the selected 1978 source, a stable calculus law is asserted without its base conditions, or an old survey ceiling leaves a required proof unwritten.

related.reason: The stable/simple/NIP comparison is a separate extension, not an assumed proof of the stable calculus.

setup: First-order compactness, Skolem expansions and ordered finite-tuple types
The exact finite or infinite Ramsey partition theorem used in each construction

components.text: Define ordered indiscernibles and carry out the finite satisfiability/compactness construction with the exact tuple-order conditions.
Prove the selected Ramsey partition lemma at its actual finite/infinite arity and color regime and identify the precise application in the construction.
Define a coherent quantifier-free Skolem blueprint, construct the generated model, and prove the induced elementary/automorphism maps at the source's stated scope.
Incorporate Hodges's p. 547 weakened Th(F) assertion and p. 563 regularity correction in the exact affected claims and proofs.
Give the nonisomorphic-model application and separate the stronger currently displayed unstable-spectrum theorem and its Shelah 1971 proof dependency from the original EM construction.

profiles.failure: A sequence is called a coherent blueprint without proving coherence, a stronger corrected-away Hodges claim is retained, or the maximal spectrum is inferred from indiscernibles alone.

additional.extent: The actual maximal uncountable spectrum result and full argument needed by thm:p03-unstable-spectrum, printed 473-487, preserving its own hypotheses.

setup: Dense ordered structures with the chosen language and parameters; definable sets and functions
Cell induction, definable continuity and semialgebraic/RCF language conventions

components.text: Define o-minimality at structure and theory levels and preserve the sources' parameter and elementary-transfer assumptions.
Prove the monotonicity theorem with every constant/increasing/decreasing and continuity interval case.
Define cells in every dimension and prove the finite compatible cell decomposition and required continuity refinements by complete induction.
Reconstruct the separate three-author Part II presentation and its actual uniformity and elementary-transfer conclusions, without substituting Part I.
Work out the RCF/semialgebraic example and explain the exact hypotheses that distinguish o-minimal tameness from NIP alone.

profiles.failure: Part II disappears into Part I, one dimension or interval case is omitted, or NIP alone is used to infer monotonicity or cell decomposition.

related.reason: The NIP comparison uses the exact o-minimal theorem regime and cannot supply its geometric proof.

setup: Formula families, shattering and type spaces with finite tuple and parameter conventions
Dividing, forking and local character in the stated saturated ambient model

components.text: Define IP/NIP for a formula and for a complete theory and prove the chosen shattering/type-count characterizations with the quantifiers explicit.
Reconstruct the actual 1971 Stability, f.c.p., and Superstability presentation selected by this goal and distinguish both other same-year Shelah papers.
Define simple theory through the actual tree/local-character equivalence selected by the text and prove the needed dividing/forking facts and base bounds.
Prove the displayed stable-to-NIP, stable-to-simple and simple-plus-NIP-to-stable relationships at theory level.
Verify the random graph as simple unstable IP and DLO/RCF as o-minimal NIP unstable, giving the actual witnessing and nonwitnessing arguments.
Complete the dividing-line comparison table and separate a single NIP formula in an arbitrary theory from Simon's later ambient-NIP-theory results.

profiles.failure: A later simple-theory result is attributed to a title-only 1971 match, formula NIP is substituted for theory NIP, or an example's required property is left unsupported.

related.reason: Reuse stable-theory definitions with exact parameter conventions; determine actual proof imports when completing the source proofs.
RCF and o-minimal examples use the separately bounded geometric development.

additional.extent: The exact simple-theory forking/dividing and local-character results used by the current simple-theory entry, with their full supporting proof extent in Forking in Simple Unstable Theories.

setup: Nonempty first-order structures, functions/relations/equality and positive formulas with the stated truth/falsity conventions
Diagrams, compactness, substructure embeddings, arbitrary substructure-chain unions and surjective homomorphisms

components.text: Prove the elementary-class substructure/universal-axiomatization equivalence and the corresponding sentence extension/existential formulation.
Prove the arbitrary substructure-chain union to universal-existential axiomatization characterization in both directions, distinguishing elementary chains.
Prove Lyndon's positive-formula preservation under surjective homomorphisms, preserving Q-map, function, equality and relative-theory conventions.
Supply the exact positive/negative occurrence interpolation lemma imported by the preservation paper and show its use in the argument.
Give the syntax/semantic-operation lookup comparison and counterexamples separating arbitrary homomorphisms with existential-positive formulas from the surjective-positive theorem.
State the all-structures regime and identify why finite-only preservation variants cannot replace these proofs.

profiles.failure: Lyndon positivity is replaced by predicate monotonicity or arbitrary-homomorphism preservation, or a sentence/class or chain-regime hypothesis is silently changed.

additional.extent: The polarity-preserving interpolation result and the exact proof lemmas explicitly imported by Properties Preserved under Homomorphism; printed 129-142 is a separate source.

setup: First-order embeddings, elementary diagrams, parameter expansions and existential closure
Algebraic closure for fixed-characteristic fields and real closure for ordered fields in the exact chosen languages

components.text: Define model completeness, existential closure, companion and completion and distinguish each from quantifier elimination.
Prove Robinson's model-completeness test and the existential-normal-form/diagram bridges in both directions.
Prove the selected existence/uniqueness and embedding facts for model companions and completions, with completeness over each expanded diagram explicit.
Give ACF as the selected model completion/companion of fields with characteristic and ring-language assumptions fixed, including the algebraic closure and elimination steps.
Give the ordered-field/RCF construction in the ordered-ring language, including real-closure existence, diagram completeness and the appropriate elimination result.

profiles.failure: The 1956 joint-consistency article replaces Complete Theories, companion is equated with completion without conditions, or a field example omits characteristic/order/language hypotheses.

setup: Compatible common signatures with matching symbol arities/kinds and shared equality
Compactness, elementary diagrams, reduct/expansion extension and Craig interpolation in the exact common language

components.text: Preserve and fully bind the elementary-reduct extension lemma and prove Robinson joint consistency under the no-contrary-common-sentence condition.
Define ordinary implicit and explicit definability for a new relation of finite arity including arity zero and prove Beth with the finite theory fragment and reduct language explicit.
Prove both Craig-to-Robinson and Robinson-to-Craig implications at the stated language/theory scope.
Prove the direction from either equivalent property to ordinary Beth while retaining the already corrected absence of a general converse from ordinary Beth.
Compare the separate 1956 Robinson article, 1953 Beth article and corrected 1993 textbook presentations and link each to its own complete statement/proof extent.

profiles.failure: The corrected result is changed back to a three-way equivalence, ordinary Beth becomes projective Beth, or compatible theories are confused with fixed-model amalgamation.

setup: Ultrafilters, products and quotient interpretations with nonempty factors and the stated selection assumptions
Los truth induction, Boolean prime ideal theorem/ultrafilter lemma and explicitly separated use of full Choice

components.text: Give the exact ultraproduct/ultrapower definitions and truth proof with each witness-selection and ultrafilter existence assumption identified.
Reconstruct Keisler's 1961 journal conditional isomorphism construction at its actual continuum/cardinality hypotheses, preserving the separate thesis identity.
Prove the Keisler-Shelah equivalence using the 1971 without-GCH construction and the converse from Los, without inventing a fixed index/filter or nonprincipality claim.
Explain BPI/ultrafilter-lemma equivalence, its relation to AC and the exact assumptions of the selected textbook construction, using separate evidence for strictness.
Give the ultraproduct compactness application and directly correct the active Los citation while preserving bibliographic correction provenance outside the reader's derivation.

profiles.failure: Keisler's historical hypotheses are removed using Shelah's later result, arbitrary fixed ultrapowers are claimed isomorphic, or BPI and full AC are conflated.

additional.extent: The precise BPI/ultrafilter-lemma equivalence and nonimplication/strictness entries required by the displayed choice boundary, including their exact metatheoretic assumptions.
The actual 1955 ultraproduct contribution, 98-113, for Los truth theorem attribution and the selected original proof extent; not On the Extending of Models I.
